title: Polynomial-time visit table
statement: For every finite-state binary Turing machine $M$ and natural numbers $C,e,c,A,d$, the function that sends a Boolean word $x$ to the table of visit rows for $M,C,e,x$, with count $c\,(A(|x|+C(|x|+1)^e+1)^d+1)^2+1$, is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: A finite-state binary Turing machine M
Natural-number parameters C, e, c, A, and d
replaced: For every source machine and parameters $C, e, c, A, d$, the function sending an instance $x$ to the ordered table of visit rows for all times up to the producer horizon plus one is polynomial-time computable: the retained instance and empty table start the loop, a clean call executes each full row step, the repetition controller runs the exact unary number of calls with a quadratic bound on all intermediate state words, and a native projection returns precisely the stored rows.
